title: Recover a set-valued topos point from sheafified representables
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with finite limits [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], and let $p:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. For $U\in\mathcal C$ let $h_U(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(T,U)$, let $h_U^\#$ be its sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and put $u(U)=p^{-1}(h_U^\#)$. Then $u$ preserves finite limits, and for every covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ the maps $u(U_i)\to u(U)$ are jointly surjective. Let $\mathcal N_u$ have objects $(U,a)$ with $a\in u(U)$ and arrows $f:(U,a)\to(V,b)$ given by arrows $f:U\to V$ satisfying $u(f)(a)=b$. This category is small and cofiltered. For every sheaf of sets $F$ the canonical map
$$\varinjlim_{(U,a)\in\mathcal N_u^{\mathrm{op}}} F(U)\longrightarrow p^{-1}F,$$
sending a section $t:h_U^\#\to F$ at $(U,a)$ to $p^{-1}(t)(a)$, is a bijection natural in $F$. Colimits and cofilteredness use [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

proof.text: First prove terminal preservation without exact sheafification: the terminal representable is already a sheaf, its reflection unit is invertible, the inclusion reflects terminal objects, and p.inverse is left exact. Prove binary-product preservation separately using small internal Homs into p.direct(E), as detailed in the following step. Combine terminal and binary-product preservation with the separate equalizer source step [lem-trf-site-point-representable-equalizers] using Mathlib preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesEqualizers_and_finiteProducts. Functor.isCofiltered_elements supplies the pointed category cofilteredness.

source.place: Tag 00YA, proof of (2), the paragraph proving condition (2) of a site point; Tag 00WJ (lemma-sheafification-exact).

proof.text: For every presheaf P and small set E, the internal Hom from P to p.direct(E), evaluated at U, is equivalent to Hom(y(U) times P, p.direct(E)). The composite sheafification and p adjunction identifies this with maps between two v-small sets, proving the internal Hom is v-small. Shrink it pointwise; it remains a sheaf by the sheaf-Hom theorem. The explicit curry/uncurry equivalence now shows that tensoring a sheafification weak equivalence f with any P induces an isomorphism after applying T = sheafification followed by p.inverse: test its maps into E via the small sheaf internal Hom. Symmetry handles either tensor factor. Thus T takes the tensor of the two sheafification units to an isomorphism. The product comparison for sheafification factors as this image followed by the invertible reflection counit. Since p.inverse preserves products, the composite product comparison is invertible. Yoneda also preserves products, giving binary-product preservation of L. This proof works with independent u and v and requires no HasSheafify assumption.

source.place: Tag 00YA (2), binary-product component of condition (2); internal-Hom/currying proof of the product step, using the two adjunctions.

proof.text: For every set E, sheafification adjunction, Yoneda and the p-adjunction identify sections of p_*E over U with functions L(U) to E. Under restriction along f this is precomposition by L(f); this follows from the two adjunction naturality identities and Yoneda naturality. These are the private sectionEquiv, directSectionEquiv, sectionHom_pre and sectionHom_post calculations.

source.place: Tags 00Y7 and 00YA, adjunction and canonical section maps.

proof.text: For a covering, suppose x in L(U) has no preimage under its pointed covering maps. Take the constant false map and the characteristic function of {x}, with values in the small set ULift Bool. Transpose both into sections of p_*(ULift Bool) over U by the preceding equivalence. Their restrictions along every covering arrow agree because none of their points maps to x. The separatedness part of the sheaf axiom makes the two sections equal. Applying the equivalence and evaluating at x says false = true, a contradiction. This includes the empty covering and uses neither local representatives nor joint epimorphy of sheafified representables.

source.place: Tag 00YA (2), covering condition; characteristic-function cancellation proof using the sheaf axiom.

proof.text: Construct the cocone with point p.inverse(F) and leg s ↦ p.inverse(sectionHom(s))(a) at (U,a). Naturality is the precomposition identity for sectionHom and the equation defining a pointed arrow. For any other cocone c, curry its legs and use directSectionEquiv inverses to construct a sheaf morphism F → p.direct(c.pt); the cocone equations are exactly its naturality. Its adjoint is the unique cocone descent. The adjunction identities prove the leg equations and, conversely, injectivity of the adjunction and section equivalences proves uniqueness. This constructs IsColimit directly with the given small point, without assuming any ambient large-index colimit exists. Take e = Iso.refl; the requested formula is reflexivity. The last naturality clause is sectionHom_post.

source.place: Tags 00YA (2) and 00Y7: the canonical comparison and the adjunction/currying description.

proof_origin.place: Tags 00YA and 00Y7. Terminal preservation uses the weak-reflection unit; binary products use pointwise-small internal Homs into p.direct(E) and explicit currying; covers use separatedness; the canonical colimit uses the adjunction. The separate 00YA equalizer component retains the arbitrary-universe exactness obligation.

split_report.summary: Split the set-valued reconstruction theorem into four complete steps: finite-limit preservation and cofiltered pointed objects, joint surjectivity over covers, the representable/skyscraper adjunction calculation, and the canonical colimit comparison for every sheaf of sets. Repaired return C1 by writing the full cancellation proof of joint epimorphy from local representatives and the sheaf equalizer axiom, then proving joint surjectivity via adjunction and characteristic functions. No new support nodes or uncited coequalizer presentation are used.

lean.statement: theorem site_point_reconstruction_sets {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (J : Precoverage C) (hJ : J.IsSiteForCoverings) [HasFiniteLimits C] [HasWeakSheafify J.toGrothendieck (Type v)] (p : GeometricMorphism (Type v) (Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (Type v))) : PreservesFiniteLimits (sitePointFunctor J p) ∧ (∀ (I : Type (max u v)) (U : C) (Ui : I → C) (f : ∀ i, Ui i ⟶ U), Presieve.ofArrows Ui f ∈ J U → ∀ x : (sitePointFunctor J p).obj U, ∃ (i : I) (y : (sitePointFunctor J p).obj (Ui i)), (sitePointFunctor J p).map (f i) y = x) ∧ IsCofiltered (sitePointNeighbourhood J p) ∧ (∀ (F : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (Type v)), ∃ (c : Cocone (sitePointSectionDiagram J p F)) (e : c.pt ≅ p.inverse.obj F), Nonempty (IsColimit c) ∧ (∀ (U : C) (a : (sitePointFunctor J p).obj U) (s : F.obj.obj (op U)), e.hom (c.ι.app (Opposite.op ⟨U, a⟩) s) = (p.inverse.map (sitePointSectionHom J F s)) a)) ∧ (∀ (F G : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck (Type v)) (α : F ⟶ G) (U : C) (s : F.obj.obj (op U)), sitePointSectionHom J G ((Sheaf.homEquiv α).app (op U) s) = sitePointSectionHom J F s ≫ α)
